notes: Draft full circuit (variant 4) from the pinned independently selected OSM node chain. Replaces the generic longest-cycle hypothesis with three connector detours; the operator variant-4 map and licensed imagery support the rounded turns and southern infield returns. Exact source coordinates, direction and phase are retained, without map tracing or fitting to an official distance. Main public timing remains missing.

source.name: Mapzen Terrain Tiles
attribution: Global elevation data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey and NOAA.
Produced using Copernicus data and information funded by the European Union, EU-DEM layers.

sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 78 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the midpoint of corresponding border stations, not an official length measurement. There is no saved GPS start gate; the simulation begins at the first trace coordinate. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

measurement.note: Estimated paired paved-road limits from the pinned licensed satellite image at approximately 0.40 m ground pixel spacing. The corrected main route follows variant 4 rounded turns and southern infield returns, rather than the superseded generic connector-detour hypothesis or variant V4b. Limits follow visible white paint/curb transitions, excluding coloured runoff, grass, fences and the parallel pit lane. At the northeastern junction, stations 324–342 follow the visible dashed white course-limit paint across the connector opening, rather than the distant outer connector edge. Shared junction openings and the main-straight pit merge are route-selection estimates rather than surveyed limits or observed continuous curbs. Other linear intervals join sparse corresponding edge pairs with a maximum 50 m observation gap. Original timing and raster terrain remain unchanged. Pixel spacing is not positional accuracy; rendered curbs remain illustrative and banking is unknown.

borderInference.note: Road-border estimates reconstructed from complete pairs of sparse image-edge measurements. Each pair defines its own road section; the original trace is preserved and constrains station displacement and route order. Linear intervals, junction openings and curbs remain estimates, not surveyed racing limits. Every saved edge station and anchor requires pinned-image coverage during authoring. No automatic evidence scores are claimed.
